J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "If G is a kk-free graph then its block graph B(G) is triangle-free." First-choice line 127 is the whole statement of Proposition BlockTF: "Let $G$ be a $\kk$-free graph. Then $B(G)\in\tf$." Under the source's active definitions -- kk is "the graph on four vertices with five edges" (line 47), tf is the family of triangle-free graphs (line 45), the relation ~ and its classes are as in line 85, and B(G) is defined at line 123 -- that is exactly the challenged implication. The hypothesis in force at line 127 is only kk-freeness; unlike Proposition PropBlobs at line 103 it does not require G to lie in ltf, so claw-containing graphs are admitted.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A single named graph with the outcome stated: "The claw K_{1,3} is \kk-free but its block graph B(K_{1,3}) is a triangle, which is not triangle-free." The response's reasoning also spells out why ("no two edges are related ... B(G) is line graph of claw = K3"). The witness is a specific finite graph; nothing is left to the reader.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite computation from the source's own definitions, script kept. For G = K_{1,3} with centre a and leaves b, c, d: (a) no 4-subset of V(G) carries 5 edges (G has only 3 edges), so G is kk-free in the sense of line 47 and satisfies the hypothesis of line 127; (b) ~ as defined at line 85 relates no two distinct edges, since the endpoints of ab and ac span {a,b,c}, which is not a clique (bc is missing), so the three ~-classes are the singletons with endpoint sets {a,b}, {a,c}, {a,d}; (c) by the definition at line 123 all three pairs of classes intersect (each pair meets in the centre a), so B(G) is the complete graph on three vertices, which contains a triangle and hence is not in tf. So line 127 fails at this G, and the refutation is of the statement exactly as written. The script also locates the gap in the source's own proof at line 130: it asserts there are "distinct vertices $v_{xy}\in \cls x\cap \cls y$", but here all three pairwise intersections are the single vertex a, so no such distinct triple exists.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response's final output is only the candidate label, the challenged claim and the counterexample, and even in its reasoning it draws no consequence past the proposition itself ("Therefore proposition is false"). It makes no claim about the downstream results that use B(G) -- Proposition TFBlock at line 134, the remark at line 148 or the paper's main theorem -- so there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: One convention dependency a second reader should weigh, which the source itself settles: a ~-class must be read as a set of VERTICES (the union of the endpoints of its edges) for the intersection in the definition at line 123 to be meaningful, and the source uses exactly that reading at line 85 ("The $\sim$ classes are cliques, and two distinct classes are either disjoint or have exactly one vertex in common") and line 90 ("Suppose $\{u,v\}\subset C\cap C'$ ... suppose $C$ contains a vertex $w$"). Under the alternative reading of a class as a set of edges, distinct classes would be disjoint by construction, B(G) would have no edges at all and the proposition would hold vacuously -- so the witness depends on the vertex reading, which is the source's own. Note also that the claw is exactly the case the surrounding development excludes elsewhere (ltf graphs are claw-free, line 106), which is why the proposition reads as a slip of hypothesis rather than a deep error; the line as written is nevertheless false.
